description:
Cześć! Jestem studentem elektroniki, który interesuje się technologiami kosmicznymi. Bardzo dobrze czuję się w programowanie w Dart/Flutter, M2M.

W tej edycji hackathonu startuję jako jednoosobowy zespół, aby w pełni sprawdzić swoje możliwości i zrealizować autorski pomysł od A do Z. Obecnie nie rekrutuję nowych członków do drużyny, ale bardzo chętnie poznam innych uczestników i wymienię się doświadczeniami w trakcie trwania wydarzenia!
summary: We developed AstroPulse, an autonomous health monitoring system combining a cross-platform, offline-first mobile application built with Dart and Flutter and a lightweight, 3D-printable wearable biometric sensor enclosure designed in Autodesk Fusion 360. AstroPulse continuously gathers critical physiological and environmental indicators—including heart rate variability, blood oxygen levels, radiation exposure, and resistance training loads—while integrating daily behavioral and mood check-ins. Using local, real-time analytics, the system evaluates anomalies and delivers immediate, actionable countermeasures without relying on Earth-based communication. During long-duration deep space missions, communication delays, cosmic radiation, altered gravity, and isolation expose astronauts to severe cardiovascular, immune, bone-loss, and psychological risks. AstroPulse empowers crew members to independently detect early health changes and protect their well-being beyond Earth's orbit.
details:
What It Does & How It Works AstroPulse is an autonomous, offline-first health monitoring system designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It operates through a continuous three-step loop: Gather, Evaluate, and Act. A wearable biometric device tracks vital physiological and environmental indicators—including heart rate variability (HRV), blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), skin temperature, cumulative radiation exposure, and resistance training loads. Data syncs locally to a crew mobile/tablet application, where onboard algorithms correlate biometric trends with daily behavioral and mood check-ins to detect early anomalies and recommend immediate, actionable countermeasures.

Benefits & Intended Impact During deep-space missions to the Moon or Mars, communication delays with Earth prevent real-time medical supervision, forcing astronauts to identify and manage health risks independently. AstroPulse provides early warnings for cardiovascular stress, immune system suppression, microgravity-induced bone density loss, and psychological fatigue caused by confinement. Beyond space exploration, this offline-first hardware and software architecture can serve patients and researchers in extreme, disconnected terrestrial environments such as polar stations, submarines, and remote expeditions.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software

Software & Programming Languages: Developed using Dart and Flutter to deliver a fast, cross-platform interface across crew tablets and wrist displays, utilizing local storage for uninterrupted offline operation.

Hardware & 3D Modeling: Designed in Autodesk Fusion 360 to create a lightweight, modular, and ergonomic sensor enclosure optimized for zero-gravity comfort and on-board 3D printing, integrated with low-power microcontroller electronics, optical biometric sensors, and dosimetry modules.

Creativity & Factors Considered Our project creatively unites custom 3D-printable hardware ergonomics with cross-platform mobile software in a single cohesive ecosystem. Key engineering factors considered during development included zero-gravity wearability, low power consumption, complete independence from Earth-based internet connectivity, and a holistic approach that treats mental and behavioral health with the same priority as physical biomarkers.
